paper_metadata.title: Accelerating the design of TiZrNbTa-based refractory high-entropy alloys with enhanced strength and ductility using machine learning and DFT calculations

evidence.quote: This study investigates the elastic and mechanical properties of TiZrNbTa-based RHEAs with alloying elements (X = Mo, Hf, V, W, Re) using a hybrid machine learning (ML) and density functional theory (DFT) approach.

The results indicate that all TiZrNbTaX RHEAs are ductile, with Hf and V improving ductility due to their lower shear moduli, while Mo, W, and Re reduce it.
Conversely, hafnium (Hf) improves ductility, as reflected in the lower B/G ratio (4.91) and reduced hardness (3.33 GPa)
The addition of Re increases resistance to deformation due to its strong atomic bonding and solid solution strengthening.

A dataset of 370 RHEAs was used to train ten ML models, with CatBoost Regressor demonstrating the highest accuracy (R² > 0.9) and lowest error metrics, making it the optimal model for predicting elastic properties.
